title: Mini Modular Production System
subtitle: Automatic Sorting Trainer Kit
summary: Automatic sorting trainer kit using Omron CP1E N40 PLC as the final thesis project for D3 Electronics Engineering.
description: A Mini Modular Production System (MMPS) designed as an automatic sorting trainer kit. The system uses an Omron CP1E N40 PLC programmed with CX-Programmer using Ladder Logic. The kit simulates a real industrial production line capable of sorting objects by material type using capacitive and inductive proximity sensors.
highlights: Omron CP1E N40 PLC as the main controller

title: PWM-Based Dual-Fan PID Humidity Control
subtitle: Arduino Terrarium Automation
summary: Closed-loop humidity control system for a terrarium using PID algorithm, PWM-driven MOSFET fans, and an ultrasonic mist maker.
description: A dual-channel humidity control system built around an Arduino microcontroller. The system reads ambient humidity via a DHT11 sensor, computes a PID correction, and drives two IRLZ44N MOSFET-switched fans via PWM to exhaust excess moisture. An ultrasonic mist maker adds humidity when needed. The system maintains a stable setpoint suitable for reptile or plant terrariums.
highlights: PID control loop with tunable Kp, Ki, Kd
IRLZ44N MOSFET for PWM fan control
Ultrasonic mist maker for humidity injection
Web-based SCADA dashboard via Web Serial API

title: Supervisory HIL SCADA Dashboard
subtitle: Real-time Web-based Control Interface
summary: A professional, real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop SCADA dashboard built with vanilla JS, Web Serial API, and Chart.js.
description: A browser-based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) dashboard designed for Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing. The interface connects directly to an Arduino via the Web Serial API, visualizes live sensor data with Chart.js charts, and allows real-time parameter tuning. The UI features a dark professional aesthetic with restrained neon accents.
highlights: Real-time serial communication via Web Serial API
PID parameter tuning via UI sliders
No backend required — pure browser app

title: RFID-Based Security Gate
subtitle: Access Control System
summary: An RFID-based automatic gate system that grants or denies access based on registered card UIDs.
description: An embedded access control system using an RC522 RFID reader connected to an Arduino. Registered card UIDs are stored in memory; a valid scan triggers a servo motor to open the gate while an LCD displays the access status. Unauthorized cards trigger a buzzer alert.
highlights: RC522 RFID module with UID-based authentication

title: LDR Analog Switch
subtitle: Light-Controlled Relay Simulation
summary: A light-dependent relay switch circuit designed and simulated in Proteus 8, using an LDR and op-amp comparator.
description: A light-sensing automatic switch circuit simulated in Proteus 8. An LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) feeds into an op-amp configured as a comparator. When ambient light drops below a threshold, the comparator output switches a relay to activate a load. The circuit was designed, simulated, and validated entirely in Proteus 8 Professional.
